p: At the siyum of a masechta we mention
the names of the ten sons of Rav Papa.
And at the end of a teshuvah
that they allude to the Aseres HaDibros;
דְּכֻלָּם הָיוּ בְּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא אֶחָד,
that they were all sons of one Rav Papa.
But in Sefer HaEshkol it is explained
שֶׁלֹּא הָיוּ כֻלָּם בְּנֵי רַב פָּפָּא אֶחָד
that they were not all sons of one Rav Papa;
rather, they are all mentioned in Shas,
and their father's name was Rav Papa,
but it was not one and the same.
And it is brought there that they have a received allusion:
וְאַתָּה אֶת בְּרִיתִי תִשְׁמוֹר (בְּרֵאשִׁית יז, ט)
but he did not explain what is alluded to in this.
וְנִרְאֶה שָׁם שֶׁהָיָה מִנְהָג זֶה מֵהַגְּאוֹנִים
And it appears there that this custom dates from the Geonim,
and even earlier, from the time of the Gemara.
And the Rema, zichrono livracha, wrote
פֶּה אֶל פֶּה אֲדַבֶּר בּוֹ (בַּמִּדְבָּר יב, ח).
“Mouth to mouth I speak with him” (Bamidbar 12:8);
וּפֶה אֶל פֶּה רָאשֵׁי תֵבוֹת פָּפָּא.
and peh el peh are the initials of PaPA.
אֲבָל נִרְאֶה עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ
But it appears, based on what Chazal say in the Midrash
changed their garb in a time of persecution;
אָמַר לָהֶם אִם אַתֶּם בָּנֶיהָ שֶׁל תּוֹרָה
and said to them: If you are sons of the Torah,
give your lives for it, etc.;
they said to him: We are its sons, etc.”
And the concept of “sons of the Torah”
הוּא עַל פִּי מַה שֶּׁכָּתוּב בַּזּוֹהַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ
is based on what is written in the holy Zohar
יִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד.
Yisrael, the Torah, and Kudsha Brich Hu are one.
וּבְפָרָשַׁת בְּשַׁלַּח (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב ס, א)
וְכִי מַאן יָהִיב לְהוּ אוֹרַיְיתָא הָכָא וְכוּלֵּי
but who gave them the Torah here? etc.”;
וּמַסִּיק דְּקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא תּוֹרָה אִיקְרֵי
and it concludes that Kudsha Brich Hu is called Torah:
וְאֵין תּוֹרָה אֶלָּא קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא,
and Torah means only Kudsha Brich Hu.
the sons of Hakadosh Baruch Hu.
and Tosafos bring from the Yerushalmi
that a woman can conceive and conceive again
and they explain: a hundred papei, fathers,
and one nanai, a dog — see there.
And they are called bar Papa: Papa is Father,
and that is Hakadosh Baruch Hu;
כָּל הַנֶּהֱנֶה מֵעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלֹא בְרָכָה
“Whoever benefits from this world without a berachah
כְּאִלּוּ גּוֹזֵל לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא וּכְנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל
is as if he robs Hakadosh Baruch Hu and Knesses Yisrael,
‘He who robs his father and his mother, etc.’;
וְאֵין אָבִיו אֶלָּא הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
and ‘his father’ is none other than Hakadosh Baruch Hu,
and ‘his mother’ is none other than Knesses Yisrael,
שְׁמַע וְגוֹמֵר וְאַל תִּטּוֹשׁ תּוֹרַת אִמֶּךָ
‘Hear, etc., and do not forsake the Torah of your mother.’”
וְתוֹרַת אִמֶּךָ הַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
And “the Torah of your mother” is Torah she'b'al peh;
וְעַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁאָמְרוּ (פְּסָחִים קיח, ב)
and along the lines of what Chazal say (Pesachim 118b):
אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
“Knesses Yisrael said before Hakadosh Baruch Hu:
רִבּוֹנוֹ שֶׁל עוֹלָם עֲשָׂאוּנִי בָנֶיךָ וְכוּלֵּי
Ribbono shel Olam, Your children have made me, etc.”
And about whom did she say “Your children”?
that the elders and the distinguished ones said it
עַל שֶׁאֵינָם חֲשׁוּבִים כָּל כָּךְ וְכוּלֵּי
about those who are not so distinguished, etc.
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁכְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל רוֹמֵז עַל גְּדוֹלֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
This means that Knesses Yisrael alludes to the great ones of Yisrael,
And when one benefits without a berachah
for one who benefits from this world without a berachah
is as if he benefited from what is consecrated to Heaven;
נֶאֱמַר (תְּהִלִּים כד, א) לַה׳ הָאָרֶץ וּמְלוֹאָהּ.
it says (Tehillim 24:1): “The earth and its fullness are Hashem's.”
these are the Anshei Knesses HaGedolah,
who instituted the reciting of birchos hanehenin.
And the allusion of PaPA comes:
for it is the gematria of two Names,
which together are the gematria of ninety-one;
and seventy corresponds to the seventy souls,
which is the number of Yisrael,
יַצֵּב גְּבוּלוֹת עַמִּים לְמִסְפַּר בְּנֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
“He set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of Bnei Yisrael”
and likewise the seventy faces of the Torah;
and ninety-one plus seventy is one hundred sixty-one,
to the Name Ekyeh spelled out with yuds;
for the Name Ekyeh alludes to the secret of Keser,
which alludes to the future to come,
and it is the beginning of Thought,
and it is the place where there is no forgetting.
And this is the allusion that they received
אִם לֹא בְרִיתִי יוֹמָם וָלַיְלָה וְגוֹמֵר
“If not for My covenant day and night, etc.,”
and it will help against forgetting.
And as we ask right after this:
“May you not be forgotten from us, etc.”;
for once one merits being bound to the root,
then there is no more forgetting there.
And so Sefer HaEshkol writes there
וְיִשְׂרָאֵל וְאוֹרַיְיתָא וְקוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא חַד הִיא,
And Yisrael, the Torah, and Kudsha Brich Hu are one.
We find many names of people in the Torah,
וְכָל סֵפֶר דִּבְרֵי הַיָּמִים מָלֵא מִשֵּׁמוֹת
and the entire sefer Divrei HaYamim is full of names,
even names of the nations of the world;
וּמִזֶּה נִשְׁאַר דִּבְרֵי תוֹרָה לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
and these too remain words of Torah forever,
and they contain secrets and allusions.
שֶׁהָיָה מְנַשֶּׁה דּוֹרֵשׁ דְּרָשׁוֹת שֶׁל דּוֹפִי
Menasheh would expound derashos of scorn:
לֹא הָיָה לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה לִכְתּוֹב אֶלָּא
“Did Moshe have nothing to write but
‘And the sister of Lotan was Timna’ (Bereishis 36:22)
וּבֶאֱמֶת אִם יֶחְסַר אוֹת אַחַת מִתִּמְנָע
But in truth, if a single letter is missing from Timna,
just as if a letter were missing from Shema, etc.;
and in the sefarim hakedoshim there is
that allusions to Shema are hinted in this pasuk.
And likewise in Sefer Nesivos Olam
by the Maharal of Prague, zecher tzaddik livracha,
there are found many times allusions
to the name of the Amora
connected to the statement he said;
and so there are allusions in these names.
three expressions, corresponding to the three upper Sefiros.
That is: “We will return to you, and your glory is upon us,”
עַל דֶּרֶךְ מַה שֶּׁנֶּאֱמַר (דְּבָרִים כו, יז–יח)
along the lines of what it says (Devarim 26:17–18):
“You have distinguished Hashem, and Hashem has distinguished you”;
for tefillin are called pe'er, glory,
in bearing upon themselves the parashah of Shema,
in which is written “Hashem is One.”
And in the tefillin of the Master of the World it is written,
“And who is like Your people Yisrael, one nation”
שֶׁהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא מִשְׁתַּבַּח בְּשִׁבְחַיְיהוּ דְּיִשְׂרָאֵל
for Hakadosh Baruch Hu is praised through the praise of Yisrael
And this is “We will return to you, and your glory is upon us,”
which is the crown of kingship,
“Our mind is on you and your mind is on us”
that all our thoughts are for Hashem Yisbarach,
and likewise Hashem Yisbarach's are on us.
לָא נִתְנַשׁ מִינָּךְ וְלָא תִתְנְשֵׁי מִינַּן
“May we not forget you, and may you not be forgotten from us”
and the desires in the heart,
“For from it are the issues of life.”
וְכָל רְצוֹנֵינוּ רַק לְהַשֵּׁם יִתְבָּרַךְ וְתוֹרָתוֹ
All our desire is only for Hashem Yisbarach and His Torah,
and a thing on which one's life depends
And after they mentioned what corresponds to the three upper Sefiros,
which is the gematria of Havayah and Adnus
and the seventy faces of the Torah
(the gematria of seventy, the number of Bnei Yisrael,
and that is Abba and Imma) —
as we find in the holy Zohar
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב רד, א) לְעִנְיַן שַׁבָּת
the daughter is crowned with the three Avos;
וּבְרַעְיָא מְהֵימְנָא (זֹהַר חֵלֶק ג רנז, א)
and in the Ra'aya Mehemna (Zohar III 257a):
from the side of the three upper levels:
And this too is the allusion
שֶׁכָּתַב רַמָּ״א עַל פָּפָּא פֶּה אֶל פֶּה
the Rema wrote on PaPA, peh el peh,
that it alludes to Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom:
וְהַיְינוּ תּוֹרָה שֶׁבִּכְתָב וְתוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה,
this is Torah she'bichsav and Torah she'b'al peh.
פָּנִים בְּפָנִים דִּבֶּר ה׳ עִמָּכֶם וְגוֹמֵר
“Face to face Hashem spoke with you, etc.”;
el peh is Torah she'b'al peh,
כְּמוֹ שֶׁכָּתוּב (תִּקּוּנֵי זֹהַר, הַקְדָּמָה יז, א)
we call it Torah she'b'al peh”;
וְהַיְינוּ גַּם כֵּן קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא וּשְׁכִינְתֵּיהּ.
and this is also Kudsha Brich Hu and His Shechinah.
וּמֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם זָכָה לִשְׁנֵיהֶם
And Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom, merited both,
the fine points of the Torah and the fine points of the Sofrim,
and what the Sofrim would in the future innovate”;
and this is peh el peh.
And every talmid chacham great in Torah
our teacher in his generation, like Moshe in his generation.
that in every generation there is a talmid chacham
שֶׁהוּא נִיצוֹץ מִנִּשְׁמַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ עָלָיו הַשָּׁלוֹם
who is a spark of the neshamah of Moshe Rabbeinu, alav hashalom,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בַּמִּדְרָשׁ (בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה נו, ז)
as Chazal say in the Midrash (Bereishis Rabbah 56:7):
“There is no generation that does not have one like Moshe.”
וְאַחַר כָּךְ מַזְכִּירִין עֶשֶׂר בַּר פָּפָּא
And afterwards we mention the ten bar Papa,
corresponding to the form of Adam,
And the Rema, zichrono livracha, wrote
an allusion to the Aseres HaDibros,
as we say in the Haggadah of Pesach:
“Who knows ten? Ten are the Dibros,”
the Aseres HaDibros, the completeness of the Torah;
the Ten Utterances, the completeness of Creation;
(בְּזֹהַר חֵלֶק ג סוֹף יא, ב–סוֹף יב, א)
(Zohar III, end of 11b and end of 12a),
that they correspond to each other;
וּכְמוֹ דְּאִיתָא בַּגְּמָרָא (רֹאשׁ הַשָּׁנָה לב, א)
and as it says in the Gemara (Rosh Hashanah 32a):
corresponding to the Ten Utterances, etc.”
with which Hashem Yisbarach created everything.
And it says in the Gemara (Sotah 44a)
and make it ready for yourself in the field;
that one should build a house,
דָּבָר אַחֵר הָכֵן בַּחוּץ מְלַאכְתֶּךָ זֶה מִקְרָא.
Another explanation: “Prepare your work outside” — this is Mikra;
“and make it ready in the field” — this is Mishnah;
“afterwards, build your house” — this is Gemara.
and Mishnah is the rulings of halachah,
to know how to conduct oneself,
“Your word is a lamp to my feet
and a light for my path”;
and it is like planting a vineyard,
which is a means to sustaining life:
to know the conduct of all the days of his life.
“And Hashem will build you a house”
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה לוֹ בַּיִת לְעוֹלְמֵי עַד
meaning that he would have a house forever,
בֵּית דָּוִד כְּמוֹ בֵּית אַהֲרֹן בֵּית יִשְׂרָאֵל
the House of Dovid, like the House of Aharon and the House of Yisrael —
וְזֶה אַחַר וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ זֶה גְּמָרָא
this is “afterwards, build your house” — this is Gemara:
who is wholly bound up in learning Torah,
שֶׁכָּל מִי שֶׁאוֹהֵב שֵׁינָה עוֹשֶׁר וְתַעֲנוּג
that anyone who loves sleep, wealth and pleasure
אֵינוֹ יָכוֹל לִלְמוֹד תּוֹרָה שֶׁבְּעַל פֶּה
since he is a master of Gemara,
יִהְיֶה לוֹ בַּיִת בִּנְיַן עֲדֵי עַד.
he will have a house, an everlasting structure.
הָכֵן בַּחוּץ מְלַאכְתֶּךָ זֶה מִקְרָא וּמִשְׁנָה.
“Prepare your work outside” — this is Mikra and Mishnah;
“and make it ready in the field” — this is Gemara;
אַחַר וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ אֵלּוּ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
“afterwards, build your house” — these are good deeds.
שֶׁיֵּשׁ מִי שֶׁאֵין עוֹד הַגְּמָרָא תַּכְלִיתוֹ
For there is one for whom the Gemara is not yet the ultimate goal,
as Chazal say in the Gemara (Berachos 17a):
“The goal of wisdom is teshuvah and good deeds,
‘The beginning of wisdom is the fear of Hashem;
good understanding to all who do them’ —
to those who do them lishmah.”
for there is a third level,
for whom this too is not the ultimate goal —
and he expounded: “Prepare your work outside” —
this is Mikra, Mishnah and Gemara;
עַתְּדָהּ בַּשָּׂדֶה לָךְ אֵלּוּ מַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים.
“make it ready in the field” — these are good deeds;
אַחַר וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ דְּרוֹשׁ וְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר,
“afterwards, build your house” — expound and receive reward.
and not today to receive reward”;
so what is “expound and receive reward” —
on condition of receiving a reward?
But the explanation is as we said
in explaining the words of the Gemara (Berachos, there):
“You shall see your world in your lifetime”;
meaning that the reward in the future
is the grasp of the secrets of the Torah
and the knowledge of Hashem Yisbarach;
so too he will merit this:
to grasp something of that light in this world,
meaning one who grasps the Torah,
מַטְעִימִין אוֹתוֹ מִפְּרִי מַעֲשָׂיו בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה.
“they give him a taste of the fruit of his deeds in this world.”
This means that in this world
he grasps the illumination of the Torah
and the knowledge of Hashem Yisbarach as in the future;
and this is “expound and receive reward”:
the reward of a mitzvah is the mitzvah,
which is the delight and the reward
that will be in the future, in Olam Haba.
And corresponding to this, the Talmud begins with a tav
It begins with a tav, corresponding to the first level:
for since he is entirely bound up in Torah
and separated from all the pleasures of this world,
אַף שֶׁלִּבּוֹ עֲדַיִין אֵינוֹ מְזוּכָּךְ כָּל כָּךְ
even though his heart is not yet so refined,
וּמִכָּל מָקוֹם כְּבָר הִיא וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ
nevertheless it is already “build your house,”
that he will have permanence forever,
as Chazal say in the Gemara (Pesachim 50b):
“A person should always occupy himself with Torah and mitzvos
for from not lishmah he comes to lishmah.”
And they wrote in the name of the Baal Shem Tov,
that the learning should be with this intent:
that through it they will merit to come
So too a master of Talmud
who has set aside all the pleasures of this world,
and his will is to do the will of our Father in Heaven,
even though he has not yet merited lishmah,
to be “good understanding to all who do them,”
that from this there will be permanence forever.
And to this alludes the first tav,
And after this, the second level,
“good understanding to all who do them” —
וְאַחַר כָּךְ סִיּוּם הַגְּמָרָא גַּם כֵּן בְּת׳
And afterwards, the conclusion of the Gemara, also with a tav,
and sustaining life is good deeds,
וּבָנִיתָ בֵיתֶךָ זֶה דְּרוֹשׁ וְקַבֵּל שָׂכָר
and “build your house” is “expound and receive reward”:
that he merits to be a ben Olam Haba
of the secrets and perceptions of Olam Haba.
And so it is customary to say in the Kaddish:
“In the world that will be renewed, etc.,
וְיַמְלִיךְ קוּדְשָׁא בְּרִיךְ הוּא בְּמַלְכוּתֵיהּ וִיקָרֵיהּ
and Kudsha Brich Hu will reign in His kingship and His glory”:
that they merit in this world
the perception and knowledge of Hashem Yisbarach,
as Chazal say: “You shall see your world in your lifetime.”
